verdict.rationale: The SDK automatically writes session transcripts to disk and can resume them with full prior context. A SessionStore adapter can mirror those transcripts to a durable backend, so a session can be resumed on another host. However, this persistence is conversation history, not a documented mid-run checkpoint, and nothing shows a crashed run resuming exactly where it stopped, such as mid-tool-call or with in-flight state restored. missing for 10: documented crash-recovery semantics for interrupted in-progress runs, explicit checkpoint granularity (per-turn or per-tool-call state including working directory/subprocess state), independent or hands-on corroboration of resume after a crash.

support.subject: As a developer, I can checkpoint agent state so a run can resume exactly where it left off after a crash or restart

citations.quote: The SDK writes it to disk automatically so you can return to it later.
Returning to a session means the agent has full context from before: files it already read, analysis it already performed, decisions it already made.

A `SessionStore` adapter lets you mirror those transcripts to your own backend, such as an object store, a key-value store, or a database, so a session created on one host can be resumed on another host running from a matching working directory.
